rationale: Round 1 built and ran correctly, so this candidate raises obfuscation pressure while protecting lpbench's hot numeric kernels (daxpy, dgesl, dgefa, matgen dominate the 5 KB text and execute in tight loops). SUB and SPLIT stay near-maximal: they are near-free transformations that add diversity and precondition basic blocks for stronger passes. FLA gets the highest SecurityGain since control-flow flattening is the strongest structural defense for the large main/dgefa bodies, but its RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights (0.7/0.6) keep it off the innermost loops where dispatch overhead would hurt. BCF is favored moderately (0.7 security) with cost weights at 0.6 so bogus arithmetic lands mostly in cold/outer blocks rather than the FFT and LU inner loops. IBR is pushed up (0.8) to obscure branch targets with acceptable indirect-branch cost given this program's small call/branch count, and ICALL/IGV are enabled at moderate levels to hide call and global-reference structure; all CorrectnessRisk weights remain at or below 0.3 because the program's fixed-pointer numeric code (common in almabench/fftbench style sources) tolerates indirection but not aggressive transformation errors. Net effect: diversity-first, strong structural obfuscation on large functions, cost-gated on hot loops.
